If you prefer a synchronous deep dive, propose 60-90 minutes with your security and network team. Otherwise we can iterate over artifacts.

- Data classification: the traffic contains PHI and regulated identifiers; we cannot allow payloads to be routed through any public internet egress once inside our VPC.
- Logging/retention: we need logs retained for 7 years for auditability (some logs can be exported to our central SIEM).

Thanks for the ping, Marissa — reviewed Sarah's constraints and sketched an initial approach below. Attaching a draft dataflow (acmehealth_dataflow_v1.pdf) and our Redwood Private security summary (redwood_private_vpc_security_summary.pdf).

Initial feasibility notes / recommended architecture:
- Data path: run Redwood inference runtime inside a customer-controlled subnet (customer VPC) with no NAT gateway and egress routes tightly controlled. The control plane (management plane) endpoints can be limited to our control plane IPs — for customers requiring zero egress, we offer an on-prem connector variant where the control plane does not carry data payloads.
- Egress controls: ensure default route does not point to an internet gateway; disable NAT for subnets hosting inference. If Acme requires outbound-only management connectivity to allow updates, we recommend outbound-only whitelisted IP ranges and use of VPC endpoints to AWS services where applicable.
- Data residency: all processed tokens must remain within the customer VPC; we support region pinning to enforce US-only residency.
- Logging & retention: we can stream audit logs and request/response metadata to a customer-managed S3 bucket or a SIEM via VPC endpoints. We support retention policies up to 7+ years; note: storing full request payloads for 7 years has cost/regulatory implications — can configure redaction or token-level logs if needed.
- KMS/HSM: we support CMEK with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS with HSM-backed keys). For customers requiring FIPS/HSM, we can validate key policies and integration steps; production rollouts will require ARNs and IAM principals for cross-account access.
- On-prem / air-gap: our on-prem agent can be deployed in an isolated network; a synchronous transfer mechanism (sFTP / removable media) can be used for model or artifact updates if control-plane connectivity is restricted. We will need a maintenance window and documented runbooks.

Requested artifacts from Acme to proceed:
- Current dataflow diagram (we received acme_infra_constraints.pdf — please confirm it includes all ingress points).
- IP ranges / firewall rules for allowed control-plane communications (if any).
- KMS details (ARNs and whether HSM-backed required).
- Desired log export target (S3 bucket ARN or SIEM endpoint).

Proposed next steps & timeline:
1) Schedule 60-90 minute technical deep dive with Acme network/security + our solutions team (Dylan + Monica + infra eng). Suggested windows: Tue/Wed next week (Sarah suggested Tue/Wed afternoon).
2) After call: deliver updated acme-specific dataflow diagram (ETA 3 business days).
3) Draft security/implementation checklist for procurement and SOC2 evidence transfer.

If that works, I'll coordinate with your scheduler, Sarah, and send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Dylan Brooks
